correctness.rationale: For every even factor length \(n\ge4\) the forbidden 11 and 0000 patterns force one or three zeros between adjacent ones. The two parity alignments give \(L+R=1+2I(\mathrm{prefix00})+2I(\mathrm{suffix00})\), hence \(N_{101}=2K-1-n/2+I(\mathrm{prefix00})+I(\mathrm{suffix00})\). All remaining three-gram and lower-gram counts follow from explicit transition-flow identities and the 2-symbol boundaries. The substitution maps every length-m parent factor to even and odd length-2m windows with identical new weight \(m-K\) and explicitly determined boundary pairs. The six independently identified 8-letter base witnesses and the induction yield both weight values and all six boundary pairs for every dyadic \(n\ge16\), hence exactly twelve distinct 3-Abelian classes. A standalone checker using two independent generation methods and sliding full three-gram counters returned VERIFY_OK; finite checks are corroboration, not proof. Risks: convention-sensitive boundary terms or a missing factor alignment were checked explicitly, including the last zero of odd-aligned windows.

value.rationale: The paper-defined 3-Abelian complexity is a natural local-pattern invariant for automatic sequences, and the exact values for even one infinite natural family of lengths were not supplied by the directly relevant known 2-Abelian recurrence papers. The new all-even-length reconstruction lemma and complete dyadic class signatures reveal why the complexity is eventually constant at twelve along powers of two. This is an infinite structural classification, not a small numerical gain, parameter renaming, or plot interpolation. It can inform future three-block coding and automatic regularity analyses; no downstream theorem is claimed. The broader sequence at arbitrary lengths remains unclassified.
